newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to miss 1996 deficit goal - govt sources.
newsitem.headline: Germany to miss 1996 deficit goal - govt sources.

text.p: Germany will overshoot a limit on new borrowing of 70 billion marks set by Finance Minister Theo Waigel by between five and 10 billion marks, sources in the conservative coalition government said on Thursday.

The federal deficit had originally been pegged at 60 billion marks, but stubbornly high unemployment has skewed Waigel's projections. But the sources said it was still too early to predict the final budget outcome this year.

Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Wednesday that a shortfall in privatisation revenues this year totalling nine billion marks would make it difficult for Waigel to keep new borrowing on target.
Planned sales of state holdings in Lufthansa AG, Postbank AG and Autobahn Tank & Rast AG are unlikely to be completed this year, the SPD says.
SPD financial policy spokeswoman Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier, accusing Waigel of deception, alleged he was breaking the German constitution by seeking new borrowing.

The overshoot puts Germany even further away from meeting the Maastricht treaty's three percent limit on budget deficits for this year, even though Waigel has said Germany would cut the shortfall to 2.5 percent in 1997.
